rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: with White, in a game played on Lichess. The two black rooks on your second rank threaten your king, and White needs moves that Black is forced to answer.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.e2: Look at the d6 bishop: on f8, it would give check to the king on h6. But f8 is occupied by your own rook, and the g7 pawn blocks the diagonal.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.p: Find the move that takes the rook off f8 without giving Black time.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.certo: The rook goes to f6 and gives check. It leaves f8, and the square is free for the bishop.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.revela: The move is the rook to f6: it gives check and leaves f8 free for the d6 bishop.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.err.g4g5.1: The pawn gives check on g5, but the rook is still on f8, and the bishop has no square to mate from.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.err.g4g5.2: After this move, the king escapes to h5. White has no more checks, and the two black rooks keep attacking your king.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.err.g4g5.3: Back to the position: find a move with check that takes the rook off f8.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.err.d3d1.1: The d3 rook goes to d1 and defends the first rank, but it threatens nothing.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.err.d3d1.2: After this move, the black rook gives check on g2, and Black keeps attacking your king with two rooks.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.err.d3d1.3: Back to the position: find a move with check that takes the rook off f8.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.err.d3g3.1: The d3 rook goes to g3 and defends the king, but the f8 rook is still in the bishop's way.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.err.d3g3.2: After this move, the g7 pawn goes to g5. Black gains time to attack with the rooks and is better.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.err.d3g3.3: Back to the position: find a move with check that takes the rook off f8.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not free f8. Find a move with the f8 rook.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: the f8 rook sits on the square the bishop needs.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.l1: The king has no square: g5 and h5 are guarded by the white pawns, and g6 by the f5 pawn. Black captures the rook with the g7 pawn; blocking the check on g6 leads to the same mate.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.l2: The g7 pawn captures the rook. By doing so, it also leaves the bishop's diagonal.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.l3: The bishop goes to f8 and gives mate: the king has no free square.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex1.l4: This is clearance: one of your pieces sits on the square or line another piece needs, and you move it away with a move your opponent must answer. Here the rook left with check, and was given up.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: again with White, in another game on Lichess. The f4 bishop would mate on d6, but your e5 knight is on the diagonal, between it and d6.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.p: Find the knight move that opens the bishop's diagonal without giving Black time.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.certo: The knight captures the g6 pawn and gives check. By leaving e5, it opens the f4 bishop's diagonal to d6.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.revela: The move is the knight to g6: it captures the pawn with check and opens the f4 bishop's diagonal.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.err.e5f7.1: The knight leaves e5, opens the diagonal and attacks the d8 rook, but it gives no check: Black has a free move.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.err.e5f7.2: After this move, the d8 rook captures the d7 pawn. Now it guards d6 and e7, and the king gains e8: the mate is gone, and Black is better.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.err.e5f7.3: Back to the position: find the knight move your opponent must answer.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.err.f4g5.1: The bishop goes to g5 and attacks the d8 rook, but the e5 knight is left undefended.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.err.f4g5.2: After this move, the g7 bishop captures the e5 knight, and Black is two rooks up.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.err.f4g5.3: Back to the position: find the knight move your opponent must answer.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.err.e5g4.1: The knight leaves e5 and opens the diagonal, but it gives no check.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.err.e5g4.2: After this move, the king goes to e7 and leaves the mating square. The bishop on d6 no longer mates, and Black is better.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.err.e5g4.3: Back to the position: find the knight move your opponent must answer.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.err.f4d2.1: The bishop leaves f4 and attacks the c3 rook, but the e5 knight is left undefended.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.err.f4d2.2: After this move, the g7 bishop captures the e5 knight, and Black is two rooks up.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.err.f4d2.3: Back to the position: find the knight move your opponent must answer.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not open the f4 bishop's diagonal. Find a move with the e5 knight.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: the e5 knight stands between the bishop and d6.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.l1: The king has no square: e8 is guarded by the d7 pawn, f7 and g8 by the e6 bishop, and e7 by the knight. Black captures the knight.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.l2: The h7 pawn captures the knight.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.l3: The bishop goes to d6 along the open diagonal and gives mate.
rot.clearance.ideia.ex2.l4: This time the piece in the way was on a line, not on the mating square. In positions like this, the piece that leaves must leave with check or a capture, so your opponent has no time to defend.
rot.clearance.demos.dama.1: Attack: now let us think from Black's side, in a game on Lichess. The d6 bishop aims at h2, next to the white king, but your queen on g3 is in the way.
rot.clearance.demos.dama.2: The queen goes to e1 and gives check. It leaves g3, and the bishop's diagonal to h2 is open.
rot.clearance.demos.dama.3: White blocks the check with the rook on f1: the king has no other way out.
rot.clearance.demos.dama.4: The bishop gives check on h2, protected by the g4 knight.
rot.clearance.demos.dama.5: The king goes to h1, the only free square.
rot.clearance.demos.dama.6: The queen captures the f1 rook and gives mate. It left the bishop's way with check, and White had no time to defend.
rot.clearance.demos.coluna.1: Attack: with White, in another game on Lichess. The f1 rook would mate on f8, but your f6 rook and the black f7 pawn block the file.
rot.clearance.demos.coluna.2: The f6 rook captures the g6 pawn and gives check. It leaves the f-file.
rot.clearance.demos.coluna.3: The f7 pawn captures the rook, and the f-file is open up to f8.
rot.clearance.demos.coluna.4: The rook goes to f8 and gives mate, protected by the h6 queen. The front rook left with check and also pulled the f7 pawn out of the way.
rot.clearance.demos.excecao.1: Attack: now with Black, in another game on Lichess. The e8 rook would land on e2 with check, but your e3 bishop blocks the file. Is it worth moving the bishop any way at all?
rot.clearance.demos.excecao.2: The bishop goes to b6, with no check and no capture. The e-file is open.
rot.clearance.demos.excecao.3: White has time to defend: the d6 rook goes to d2 and guards e2. The game is equal.
rot.clearance.demos.excecao.4: Back to the position: the bishop can leave by capturing the c1 bishop. That way, White must recapture and has no time to guard e2.
rot.clearance.demos.excecao.5: The bishop captures the c1 bishop, and the e-file is open.
rot.clearance.demos.excecao.6: White recaptures with the a1 rook. Otherwise, they would lose the extra piece they had.
rot.clearance.demos.excecao.7: The rook lands on e2 and gives check. The h2 knight is attacked by the h5 rook and defended only by the king.
rot.clearance.demos.excecao.8: The king steps out of check to g1. Now both black rooks attack the h2 knight, and only the king defends it.
rot.clearance.demos.excecao.9: The e2 rook captures the knight, and the king cannot recapture: the h5 rook protects h2. Before clearing, check that the piece leaves with tempo, that the blow works and that nothing is more urgent.
rot.clearance.pratica.valeAqui.enunciado: Your queen can give check on h7, protected by the d3 bishop. Is it worth it here? Play as White and find the best move.
rot.clearance.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The check on h7 won nothing. The queen captured the d4 rook and, after the trade, the bishop left the d-file with check on h7: the d1 rook wins the queen.
rot.clearance.pratica.valeAqui.err.e4h7: The queen gives check on h7, but the king goes to f8, and the d4 rook keeps attacking: Black is better. First see what the d4 rook attacks.
rot.clearance.pratica.valeAqui.err.e4e3: The queen steps out of the rook's attack, but Black keeps the rook on d4 and is better. First see whether the d4 rook can be captured.
rot.clearance.pratica.casa.enunciado: Now it is your turn. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.clearance.pratica.casa.fim: The rook left g7 with check on h7 and freed g7. Black captured the rook, and the queen came to g7 with mate, protected by the h6 bishop.
rot.clearance.pratica.casa.err.f3e4: The pawn captures the bishop, but it gives no check: the d4 knight goes to e6 and guards g7, and the game is equal. Find the rook move that frees g7 for the queen.
rot.clearance.pratica.casa.err.g7f7: The rook leaves g7, but with no check, and Black gains time to attack your king and is much better. Find a move with check.
rot.clearance.pratica.casa.err.g7g8: The rook gives check on g8, but the d8 rook captures it, and Black is a rook up. Find the move with check that leaves g7 free for the queen.
rot.clearance.pratica.linha.enunciado: Play as White and find the best move.
rot.clearance.pratica.linha.fim: The bishop left the d-file with check on c5. The black queen captured it, and the d1 rook came to d8 with mate.
rot.clearance.pratica.linha.err.b3c4: The pawn captures the queen, but the knight comes to d7 and attacks the e5 rook, and the g4 bishop already attacks the d1 rook: Black is better. First look for a move with check.
rot.clearance.pratica.linha.err2.e5c5: The e5 rook captures the queen, but it gives no check, and Black gains time: the g4 bishop attacks the d1 rook. Look at the d-file, which the bishop left free.
